newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-SELES LATEST WOMEN'S SEED TO FALL AT WIMBLEDON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SELES LATEST WOMEN'S SEED TO FALL AT WIMBLEDON.

text.p: Monica Seles squandered a match point on Monday as unseeded Frenchwoman Sandrine Testud completed an astonishing comeback by knocking the second seed out of the Wimbledon tennis championships.
Testud did not take a game until 37 minutes into the match but gained strength and confidence, while Seles visibly tired, to win the third round match 0-6 6-4 8-6.
Seles, who dropped a match point at 6-5 in the final set, was the eighth women's seed to fall with six knocked out on Sunday's extra day alone.
"I was playing so well in the first set and at the beginning of the second," Seles said. "I was up 5-2 then I had the match point...I should never have let her back into the match."
Seles has had problems on and off court during the rain-ravaged championships.
On court she has looked overweight and cumbersome and on Monday she mis-hit at crucial times on a dull, grey but mercifully dry day.
"I am not timing my backhand as I usually do and that let me down on the key points today," she said.
Off the court, Seles has been increasingly concerned by her father's battle against cancer and hurt by the publication of unflattering pictures in the British press highlighting her added weight.

Seles had been concerned about her timing during a three-set victory over American Kristina Brandi on Sunday but her game appeared in good shape when play began on time at 1000GMT on the outside courts at the start of the second week of the championships.
She swept through the first set in half an hour before Testud lifted her game, matching the American's ground strokes on a court where the bounce was slow and often disconcertingly low.
"I missed a couple of shots that she was out of contention of getting and they were key shots a few times," Seles said. "She started serving really well."

By contrast, third seed Jana Novotna had her easiest match of the championships so far, beating Spaniard Gala Leon Garcia 6-4 6-2 to reach a fourth-round appointment with 11th-seeded American Mary Joe Fernandez.
Novotna, taken to three sets in both the previous rounds, did not lose concentration this time although she needed five set points to close off the first set.
In the second set, the Czech raced to a 4-1 lead as the dispirited Leon Garcia began hitting more and more errors and in the final three games Novotna conceded only two points.

Novotna, a favourite with the Centre Court crowd since she sobbed on the shoulder of the Duchess of Kent after throwing away the lead to lose the 1993 final to Steffi Graf, said the court was badly damaged after the first week's rain.
"It changes the whole time, you have to approach (the net) through the middle because there is a path there and you never get a decent bounce," she said.
Three times men's champion Boris Becker did not need to break into a sweat as he defeated Briton Mark Petchey 6-3 6-3 6-2. The German has yet to drop a sets in three rounds .
"I feel like I'm playing at match level," Becker said. "You never expect easy matches but you take them when they come along."
